newsitem.title: UK: Wet Brent posts recent high in tight N.Sea market.
newsitem.headline: Wet Brent posts recent high in tight N.Sea market.

text.p: Brent crude changed hands at a fresh high on Wednesday with a tight prompt market, absent Iraqi barrels and paper positions boosting values, traders said.
An August 4-6 loading cargo moved to a refiner at August plus 15 cents, five cents higher than a deal on Tuesday and 10 cents above Monday's transaction.

Traders said the deal appeared partly to be a reflection of the buyer's long swaps position. They speculated the buyer, who now has at least four cargoes loading in the same date range, had shorts to a U.S. refiner offering Brent cargoes to customers in the U.S. Gulf at September WTI minus five cents.
The U.S. refiner failed the VLCC lined up for the transatlantic voyage but was believed to have fixed two LR2s as replacements.
"If they (the refiner) don't have some deal (with the Brent buyer) then I think we'll see the market moved even higher next week," said one market observer.

Cash crude was quiet but stronger, with Aug/Sep quoted at +0.16/+0.20 and Sep/Oct gaining a few cents to trade at -4 cents. Outright values also rose after bullish U.S. industry stock data pushed up U.S. gasoline futures. September Brent was up 17 cents a barrel at $18.39 at 1745 gmt.
Other North Sea grades were dragged into more expensive territory on the back of Brent and as refiners abandoned their wait for the long-delayed arrival of Iraqi barrels.
Reports from U.N. headquarters in New York indicated an aid distribution plan, which Iraq says must be finalised before exports can resume, will not be approved before the weekend.
Traders expected that agreeing new price formulae and signing new contracts will take a further two weeks, suggesting an earliest sales start date of mid-August.
"People have been holding back waiting for Iraqi oil but they can't wait that long," said one trader.
"People are already starting to cover for the second and third decade (of August) as there is still no sign from New York or Iraq that sales will begin," said one seller.

Two Forties cargoes traded on Wednesday at a strong Dated Brent +38 cents and an Oseberg and Heidrun moved at undisclosed prices. Statfjord cargoes were offered by several sellers at a hefty 40 cent premium to Dated.
"There are still systems out there that need to buy oil and if the timing is right we think we'll get that number," said one seller.
North Sea production problems were also lending support to the market, with the Nelson field, already running below capacity, shut down on Tuesday night until at least Friday.
Saga Petroleum's 200,000 barrels per day Snorre field was shut in on Sunday because of a power failure and will not resume production until Friday.
The Statfjord programme, into which Snorre feeds, has not yet been affected, with cargoes so far just moved to load at the end of their three day date range.
One of the 11 Flotta cargoes in the August loading programme has been cancelled and the others deferred by 3-4 days because of production losses.
Short-term swaps for next week (July 28-01) firmed on the solid Brent deal, trading at +9 cents against September.
The following week (Aug 4-8) also firmed to trade at -4 cents and -7 cents.
-- Sean Maguire, London newsroom +44 171 542 8060
